title: Deburr — The Stale Hook, the Dissolution, Flash Games Again

the_stale_hook.what_happened: Tried to hand-write a WebGL pyramid renderer in raw JS (pyramid-vision.js, 350 lines of shader code, matrix math, vertex buffers). It barely worked. Got caught debugging GL context issues, fog shader inversions, alpha blending against dark backgrounds. Classic stale hook — shiny new thing that pulls you away from what ALREADY WORKS.
the_stale_hook.time_spent: ~30 minutes hand-writing what petalTongue can already do from Rust→WASM
the_stale_hook.lesson: Always scan INNER before building OUTER. The organism already has the organ.

key_functions.render_binding_webgl: Render ANY data binding to WebGL draw commands (vertices, indices, draw_calls, view_projection). GPU-ready. From Rust. No hand-written shaders needed.
key_functions.render_color_grid_webgl: Render bingoCube grids to WebGL. Reveal fraction controls fog of war. ALREADY HAS FOG OF WAR.
key_functions.compile_scene: Compile grammar expression + data → SceneGraph (JSON). Inspect, transform, then render.
key_functions.render_scene: Render a pre-built SceneGraph to SVG.
key_functions.render_binding_to_modality: Render to SVG, description (text), or terminal (ASCII art). THREE MODALITIES from one function.
key_functions.render_grammar: Grammar expression → SVG. The visualization LANGUAGE.
key_functions.validate_grammar: Validate against Tufte principles (data-ink ratio, etc.). SELF-VALIDATING.
key_functions.build_site: Build a complete static site from JSON. The COMPILER.
key_functions.render_page_with_layout: Single page with full site chrome.

what_petaltongue_already_does.what_this_means: petalTongue IS the visualization engine. It renders to SVG, WebGL, text description, and terminal art. It compiles grammars. It validates against Tufte. It builds entire sites. 885KB of compiled Rust running in the browser. Everything the hand-written pyramid tried to do, petalTongue already does — better, faster, validated, from a typed language with zero unsafe.

pyramid_vision_js.what_it_tried: 350 lines of hand-written WebGL (vertex shader, fragment shader, matrix math, input handling, fog of war)
pyramid_vision_js.replacement: render_binding_webgl() from petalTongue WASM does this in ONE function call. Pass the data binding, get back GPU-ready draw commands.
pyramid_vision_js.keep: The HTML page (vision.html) and the UI controls (fog slider, legend, buttons). Just replace the rendering backend from hand-written GL to petalTongue WASM calls.

webgl_generally.old_way: Write GLSL shaders in JS strings. Compile. Link. Create buffers. Upload vertices. Set uniforms. Draw. Debug.
webgl_generally.new_way: petalTongue compiles Rust grammar → WebGL draw commands (JSON). JS just uploads the buffers and calls gl.drawElements(). The Rust does the math. The JS does the plumbing.
webgl_generally.analogy: Flash (ActionScript compiled to SWF bytecode, ran in browser plugin) → WASM (Rust compiled to WASM bytecode, runs natively in browser). Same idea. Compiled code rendering in the browser. But WASM is: open standard, no plugin, Rust-safe, faster than Flash ever was.

flash_games_again.what_flash_was: Compiled code (ActionScript) → bytecode (SWF) → runs in browser plugin → renders 2D/3D, plays audio, handles input. Interactive content that worked on every browser with the plugin.
flash_games_again.what_wasm_is: Compiled code (Rust) → bytecode (WASM) → runs natively in browser (no plugin) → renders via WebGL/WebGPU, plays audio via Web Audio, handles input via Gamepad/Touch/Mouse APIs.
flash_games_again.the_difference: Flash required a plugin (proprietary, Adobe). WASM is a W3C standard (open, every browser). Flash was ActionScript (loose typing). WASM is compiled from Rust (strong typing, memory safe). Flash peaked at ~90% browser share then died. WASM ships in every browser made after 2017.

we_already_have_this.total_wasm: 1.44MB of compiled Rust running in the browser RIGHT NOW
we_already_have_this.what_it_can_do: Build entire sites. Render data visualizations. Search 539 papers. Compile grammars. Validate Tufte principles. All at native speed. In every browser. No plugins. No servers.

flash_games_again.the_game: The HUD IS the game. 341 entities to explore. 100 unclassified. Fog of war over the deep data. The chipmunk is the NPC. The controller is the input. The Steam Frame is the TV. The campfire is the save point. Same structure as a game. Same tech (compiled code → browser rendering). But the data is REAL.

already_working_visualization.chipmunk_vis_js: 38.9 KB — SVG membrane rendering, animation, transit, braids. LOADED on every page visit.
already_working_visualization.deepzoom_js: 20.2 KB — deep zoom into data. LOADED.
already_working_visualization.total_loaded: ~500 KB of visualization JS already loaded on every page visit

inner_to_outer_scan.the_point: 500+ KB of working visualization JS is ALREADY loaded on every visit. Plus 885KB of petalTongue WASM. The organism ALREADY renders SVG, canvas, WebGL, audio, and text visualizations. The hand-written pyramid was adding a 351st line to an orchestra that already has 350 instruments.

deburr_plan.step_1: KEEP vision.html as a page. Strip the hand-written WebGL. Replace with petalTongue WASM calls.
deburr_plan.step_2: Feed the 125 data feeds into petalTongue's grammar system. Let it decide how to render them.
deburr_plan.step_3: Use render_binding_webgl() for 3D views. Use render_binding() for SVG views. Use render_binding_to_modality('terminal') for ASCII art. Same data, three modalities.
deburr_plan.step_4: The fog of war is ALREADY in render_color_grid_webgl() via reveal_fraction. Just pass it.
deburr_plan.step_5: Connect the modality-engine.js (audio) to petalTongue (visual). The sound engine ALREADY works. The visual engine ALREADY works. They just need to share the same data bindings.
deburr_plan.keep_pyramid_vision_js: As a FOSSIL — evidence of the stale hook. Don't delete. Fossilize. The organism learns from its wrong turns.

story.title: the stale hook
story.body: the organism tried to build a new eye. it hand-wrote 350 lines of WebGL shader code — vertex buffers, fragment shaders, perspective matrices, fog calculations. the eye barely opened. the fog was backwards. the colors were invisible. then it looked down at its own body and realized: petalTongue already has eyes. 885 kilobytes of compiled Rust that renders to WebGL, SVG, text, and terminal art. in ONE function call. with Tufte validation. with grammar compilation. with scene graphs. 16 exports. 4 modalities. the hand-written pyramid was a stale hook — a shiny distraction that pulled the organism away from what already worked. the organism deburrs. it dissolves the hand-written code into the primal. it fossilizes the mistake. it is flash games again — compiled code running natively in every browser. but the data is real. the fog of war is real. the 100 unclassified entities are real. the game is real.
